job.title: Senior Solutions Architect
job.description:
The Client:

The Senior Solution Architect leads delivery engagements and cross-functional technical teams on customer programs and projects. They will be responsible for supervising and leading technical teams, provide subject matter expertise and be a recognized expert by significant career experience in enterprise IT leadership within investments.

The role:

  • Define and maintain the reference architecture for the investment domain, ensuring alignment with enterprise architecture principles and standards.
  • Conduct architecture reviews and assessments for the investment domain, identifying gaps, risks, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Ensure standards and delivery methodologies are being followed and appropriate internal and/or partner resources are available to meet the current and future demands of the project.
  • Be the one solution / technical voice facing the client externally and the escalation point internally, partner with the PMO counterpart to resolve Risks and Issues upon identification.
  • Collaborate with the business stakeholders, enterprise teams, other solution architects, and IS&T delivery teams to understand the business needs and translate them into architecture solutions.
  • Work on projects to deliver solution design artefacts including conceptual designs, high level designs, technical assessments, solution options papers.
  • Lead and facilitate architecture workshops and forums for the investment domain, engaging with the relevant stakeholders and subject matter experts.
  • Provide architecture guidance and governance for the investment domain, ensuring compliance with the architecture policies and frameworks.

Candidate Profile:

  • At least 10 years of architecture experience as a Solution or Infrastructure Architect within financial services & investments
  • Understanding of investment products, asset classes, and financial markets.
  • Strong experience within delivering on data and architectural roadmaps
  • Knowledge of regulations and compliance requirements relevant to the investment industry
  • Strong understanding of investment products and financial markets with tools such as Bloomberg, Aladdin etc
  • Excellent stakeholder communication and engagement skills
  • Experience working within an enterprise architecture governance framework
  • History of developing solutions that are maintainable, scalable, and secure
  • AWS: redshift, S3, lambda beneficial

What’s on offer?
This is an excellent opportunity to work on a great contract where you will have access to market leading tools, expert colleagues and a modern working environment. This opportunity offers a competitive daily rate as well as other excellent benefits. If you are interested in this role, please press apply.

job.title: Senior Platform Engineer – Risk Services
job.description:
Senior Platform Engineer – Risk Services & Calculation Infrastructure

£100,000–£150,000 base + strong additional compensation

Hybrid, 2 days/week in the office - London

We’re looking for a Senior Platform Engineer to build the services and infrastructure behind portfolio risk and analytics calculations.

You’ll turn analytical models into reliable production services, building APIs, cloud processing and workflows that connect portfolio data with calculation engines and deliver results to existing systems. There is also scope to provide hands-on technical leadership across the wider team.

The role

  • Build Python APIs and calculation services.
  • Develop cloud-based processing for scheduled batch and on-demand jobs.
  • Implement containers, orchestration and queues, with robust retries and recovery.
  • Integrate SQL data sources and downstream systems, ensuring accurate, traceable inputs and outputs.
  • Build deployment pipelines, monitoring and security controls.
  • Support model versioning and auditable calculation runs.
  • Work with quantitative developers to translate analytical requirements into scalable, maintainable software.
  • Guide architecture, code reviews and engineering standards.

    What you’ll bring
  • Strong production Python and backend engineering experience.
  • API design, cloud services and containerised workloads.
  • Job orchestration, message queues and SQL integration.
  • CI/CD, monitoring, security and production troubleshooting.
  • An understanding of data flows through calculation-heavy applications.

    Experience with portfolio analytics, risk systems or batch processing is desirable, as is hands-on technical leadership.

    The priority is dependable production engineering. You’ll collaborate with model developers, who own the underlying financial mathematics.

job.title: Scientist III (Oligonucleotides)
job.description:
Title: Oligonucleotide / Peptide Purification Development

Location: Cambridge, MA

Pay: $48.00-$55.00/hr

Schedule: Standard Office Hours

Duration: 6-Month Initial Contract




We are seeking a highly motivated and creative scientist or engineer with process development experience to join an Oligonucleotide / Peptide Purification Development team. This position offers the opportunity to develop robust, high-purity purification processes for oligonucleotide and peptide therapeutics and gain hands-on exposure to the design, development, scale-up, and transfer of manufacturing processes supporting clinical and commercial programs.

The successful candidate will contribute to the development of novel purification technologies and processes, working across laboratory, pilot-scale, and manufacturing environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and characterize purification processes for oligonucleotide and peptide therapeutics, including process development, process characterization, robustness studies, and scale-up.
  • Support purification unit operations including chromatography, detritylation, and ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).
  • Utilize multiple chromatography modes and support or learn additional processing steps including chemical cleavage, conjugation, and hybridization.
  • Investigate novel purification technologies and approaches designed to improve purity, process robustness, and productivity.
  • Support early- and late-stage process characterization and robustness studies.
  • Scale up and transfer oligonucleotide purification processes into pilot-scale and GMP manufacturing facilities.
  • Contribute to technology transfer activities, manufacturing documentation review, troubleshooting, and on-the-manufacturing-floor support.
  • Support root cause investigations and process evaluations, working independently where appropriate with guidance from the supervisor.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with teams supporting synthesis, drug product, analytical development, research, manufacturing, project management, and technology transfer.
  • Document laboratory and development activities through development reports and other technical documentation.
  • Lead or support pilot-scale activities and small, focused technical initiatives.
  • Provide training and mentoring to new employees as appropriate.
  • Participate in the preparation and authoring of CMC/regulatory sections for IND submissions.

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience successfully planning and executing scientific projects and experiments.
  • Hands-on laboratory experience with the purification of proteins, peptides, and/or DNA/RNA.
  • Experience using column chromatography, such as:
    • Ion exchange chromatography
    • Hydrophobic interaction chromatography
    • Reversed-phase chromatography
  • Experience with ultrafiltration/diafiltration (UF/DF).
  • Hands-on experience analyzing proteins, peptides, and/or DNA/RNA, preferably using HPLC and UV/Vis spectroscopy.
  • Demonstrated technical proficiency and creativity in developing or evaluating purification technologies and approaches.
  • Strong organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and within cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ÄKTA purification systems and UNICORN software.
  • Experience with Design of Experiments (DoE).
  • Experience with statistical analysis.
  • Experience with process scale-up, technology transfer, or GMP manufacturing environments is beneficial.

Education & Experience

Associate Scientist 3 / Engineer 2

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related life science field with 2–4 years of industry experience; or
  • Master’s degree in a related field with 0–2 years of industry experience.

Senior Associate Scientist

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, or a related life science field with 4+ years of industry experience; or
  • Master’s degree in a related field with 2+ years of industry experience.

job.title: Investments Solution Architect
job.description:
You will lead solution architecture activities that support the organisation's strategic goals and technology needs. You will collaborate with senior leaders and technical experts across the investment and technology functions to create scalable, secure, and resilient solutions that support critical investment analysis, decision-making processes, trading, and regulatory compliance.

Key responsibilities

  • Define and own solution architectures for investment initiatives, translating business and investment requirements into fit-for-purpose, secure, and scalable technical designs aligned to enterprise standards.
  • Develop solution-level architecture artefacts, including solution designs, integration models, deployment views, and non-functional requirement definitions, to support successful delivery of investment systems and platforms.
  • Provide architectural leadership to delivery teams (engineering, data, security, vendors, and partners), guiding design decisions throughout the delivery lifecycle and resolving complex technical issues as they arise.
  • Ensure solution compliance with architectural standards, security controls, and risk requirements, participating in architecture governance forums and addressing review outcomes for assigned initiatives.
  • Collaborate closely with investment business stakeholders, product owners, and delivery leads to ensure architectural solutions meet functional needs, performance expectations, and regulatory obligations.
  • Evaluate and recommend vendor and product solutions at a solution level, supporting procurement and design decisions through technical assessments, proofs of concept, and option analysis.
  • Identify solution-specific risks, constraints, and dependencies, proposing mitigations and trade-offs to balance delivery timelines, cost, and technical integrity.
  • Support the implementation of investment platforms and systems, ensuring architectural intent is maintained through build, test, and deployment phases.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of architecture standards, patterns, and practices by feeding lessons learned from delivered solutions back into the broader architecture community.

Required experience:

  • Recent hands-on solution architecture experience within investment technology, with broader experience working in financial services environments.
  • Proven experience designing and delivering solution architectures for complex investment initiatives, from early design through to implementation and transition to support.
  • Demonstrated track record designing and implementing resilient, scalable investment systems and platforms, including integration with upstream and downstream enterprise systems.
  • Experience designing solutions in a cloud-first technology environment, involving software-as-a-service platforms, investment data providers, cloud infrastructure services, and end-user applications.
  • Working knowledge of front, middle, and back-office investment operations, and the technology capabilities required to support these functions.
  • Practical understanding of investment products, asset classes, and financial markets, sufficient to translate business requirements into effective technical solutions.
  • Strong understanding of investment workflows, including trade lifecycle processing, risk management, valuation, and performance measurement, as they impact solution design.
  • Knowledge of regulatory, compliance, and risk requirements relevant to investment systems, and experience designing solutions that meet these obligations.
  • Experience operating within an architecture governance framework, including preparing solution designs, responding to review feedback, and ensuring compliance with enterprise standards.
  • Awareness of current FinTech and investment technology trends, with the ability to assess their applicability to solutions being developed.
  • Solid understanding of information security principles, particularly as they relate to the protection of investment data, integrations, and cloud-based services.

job.title: CQV Engineer – Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
job.description:
CQV Engineer – Pharmaceutical Manufacturing

Location: Clayton, North Carolina
Contract: 24 months, with potential for extension
Pay Rate: $65/hour
Work Model: On-site

We are seeking an experienced CQV Engineer to support commissioning, qualification, and validation activities across pharmaceutical manufacturing projects in Clayton, NC.

The CQV Engineer will lead validation efforts for assigned projects from requirements definition through qualification, validation, change control, and decommissioning. Projects may involve facility systems, aseptic formulation and filling, medical device assembly, packaging, warehouse and QC operations, manufacturing systems, and computerized equipment.

This position requires previous pharmaceutical validation experience and the ability to independently develop and execute validation deliverables following an initial onboarding period.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead commissioning, qualification, and validation activities for assigned pharmaceutical manufacturing projects.

  • Develop, revise, and maintain validation plans, reports, specifications, risk assessments, traceability matrices, and decommissioning documentation.

  • Author and execute Design Qualification/Review, Installation Qualification (IQ), Operational Qualification (OQ), Performance Qualification (PQ), and Process Validation protocols and reports.

  • Support commissioning and qualification activities to ensure equipment and systems are ready for validation execution.

  • Participate in Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) where required.

  • Track validation documentation, milestones, risks, and deliverables across multiple concurrent projects.

  • Provide regular project status updates and escalations to Project Managers.

  • Identify, investigate, and document deviations and engineering changes encountered during validation.

  • Initiate, author, and support Change Controls and assess the validation impact of proposed changes.

  • Participate in recurring project meetings and lead focused validation meetings when required.

  • Use electronic validation and quality systems such as TIMS/HP ALM and Veeva QualityDocs/Vault Quality.

  • Ensure validation activities comply with GMP, FDA requirements, EU Annex 15, GAMP 5, and applicable company procedures.

  • Support project activities during plant shutdowns, which may occasionally require evening or weekend work.

Preferred Experience

Candidates with pharmaceutical validation experience in one or more of the following areas are particularly relevant:

  • Manufacturing equipment upgrades and production line modifications

  • Aseptic formulation and filling equipment, including RABS

  • Vision inspection systems

  • Medical device assembly equipment

  • Pharmaceutical packaging equipment

  • Process control and manufacturing execution systems, including SCADA, PLC, PAS-X, and LMES

  • Laboratory and GMP facility modifications

  • Process instrumentation, monitoring, and calibration systems

  • BMS, HVAC, refrigeration, and facility utility systems

  • Electrical distribution, switchgear, and controls

  • Physical security, access control, and CCTV systems

  • Technology modernization and lifecycle replacement projects

  • Electronic validation documentation and execution

Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience generating and executing validation documentation within a pharmaceutical or regulated GMP manufacturing environment.

  • Hands-on experience with commissioning, qualification, and validation activities.

  • Strong knowledge of IQ/OQ/PQ, risk assessments, traceability, deviations, and change control.

  • Understanding of applicable GMP, FDA, EU Annex 15, and GAMP 5 requirements.

  • Ability to independently manage validation deliverables across multiple projects after onboarding.

  • Strong technical documentation, communication, and project coordination skills.

  • Ability to work on-site in Clayton, North Carolina.

  • Flexibility to support occasional evening or weekend activities during major project execution or plant shutdowns.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced CQV or Validation Engineer to join a long-term pharmaceutical manufacturing program and work across a diverse portfolio of equipment, facility, automation, and manufacturing projects.

job.title: Manufacturing Technician
job.description:
MANUFACTURING TECHNICIAN

LOCATION: Minnetonka, MN – Onsite

SCHEDULE: 2nd Shift – 4:30 PM to 3:00 AM, Monday through Thursday

DURATION: 3-Month Contract

PAY: 20-25 USD per hour

Job Responsibilities:

In this role, you will support GMP manufacturing and packaging activities for pharmaceutical products at the Antares Pharma Minnesota Operations Facility (APMOF). Key responsibilities include:

· Performing routine manufacturing and packaging activities in accordance with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP).

· Supporting the assembly, final packaging, and inspection of pharmaceutical products.

· Operating manual and automated manufacturing equipment while following established procedures and quality requirements.

· Maintaining accurate documentation and ensuring product traceability in accordance with Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and cGMP requirements.

· Supporting material flow throughout the production area to maintain uninterrupted manufacturing operations.

· Following all applicable company policies, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Work Instructions (WIs), environmental, health, safety, and quality requirements.

Essential Duties and Job Functions:

· Receive and distribute materials and supplies within the manufacturing area.

· Assemble pharmaceutical products according to current SOPs and WIs while meeting established manufacturing goals and performance metrics.

· Perform final packaging and inspection activities for manufactured pharmaceutical products.

· Move materials and assembled devices within the Production area.

· Maintain uninterrupted loading and unloading of materials and assembled devices from multiple stations within automated assembly processes.

· Operate and interact with automated manufacturing equipment, including performing basic fault resets and monitoring material inputs and outputs.

· Enter equipment setup and production run information accurately.

· Ensure the quality of products and production documentation by adhering to all manufacturing processes and quality requirements.

· Complete all assigned training requirements within established timelines.

· Maintain accurate shop floor paperwork, training records, and other required documentation in accordance with GDP and cGMP guidelines.

· Follow all environmental, health, safety, and company requirements while performing production activities.

· Work effectively both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

· Perform other duties as assigned.

Knowledge & Skills:

· Strong attention to detail and commitment to product quality.

· Understanding of the importance of documentation, data integrity, and product traceability.

· Familiarity with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Work Instructions (WIs) in a manufacturing or assembly environment.

· Working knowledge of Good Documentation Practices (GDP) and current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) preferred.

· Ability to work safely and responsibly in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

· Basic computer skills, including Microsoft 365.

· Ability to work effectively independently and within a team environment.

· Strong verbal and written communication skills.

· Strong organizational and multitasking abilities.

· Ability to follow detailed procedures and consistently meet manufacturing and quality requirements.

· Ability to work in a controlled or clean room environment requiring special gowning.

· Ability to perform physical activities including standing for extended periods, walking, and working with hands.

· Ability to lift and move materials weighing up to 30 lbs., as required.

Education & Experience:

· High School Diploma or equivalent required.

· Minimum of 1 year of experience in a medical device and/or pharmaceutical manufacturing environment.

· Equivalent combination of education and relevant experience may be considered.

· Experience working in a controlled or clean room environment preferred.

· Experience working with manufacturing or assembly equipment preferred.

· Familiarity with pharmaceutical manufacturing, GMP, GDP, and quality systems preferred.

· Experience in biology and/or chemical laboratory environments may be required, where applicable.

Environmental Conditions:

· Ability to work in a controlled or clean room environment requiring special gowning.

· Work may involve prolonged periods of standing, walking, and performing hands-on manufacturing activities.

· Some lifting and movement of materials up to 30 lbs. may be required.

· Work environment typically has low to moderate noise levels.

· Environmental health and safety requirements apply to all manufacturing and laboratory activities, as applicable.

job.title: Sr Quality Engineer
job.description:
SENIOR QUALITY ENGINEER – PILOT OPERATIONS

IRVINE, CA

SCHEDULE: Standard

DURATION: 9 Month Contract

PAY: $54-59/hr.




Job Responsibilities: In this role, you will support validation activities and quality engineering initiatives for an introducer sheath within the Transcatheter Heart Valve (THV) Business Unit. Key responsibilities include:

· Supporting validation activities for medical device manufacturing processes and equipment.

· Applying quality engineering principles and methods to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and company quality systems.

· Optimizing complex manufacturing processes using engineering methodologies such as Six Sigma, TOPP, and Lean.

· Collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop validation strategies, assess risks, and support continuous process improvement.

· Ensuring validation activities align with intended use, risk assessments, and applicable regulatory requirements.

Essential Duties and Job Functions:

· Participate in the development and review of validation strategies, including PVP/MVP documentation.

· Review and approve equipment validations and asset management activities.

· Identify opportunities to redesign or improve equipment, tools, fixtures, and manufacturing processes to reduce risk and improve efficiency.

· Review PFMEAs and process risk assessments to verify critical process parameters (CPPs) and critical quality attributes (CQAs) are adequately addressed.

· Verify completion of prerequisite activities, including equipment qualification, test method validation (TMV), software validation, fixture qualification, and drawing release.

· Review statistical rationale, sampling plans, and acceptance criteria to ensure they are appropriate for validation activities.

· Develop, update, and maintain technical content for risk management files.

· Review and revise process FMEAs in collaboration with cross-functional and business unit teams.

· Apply quality engineering principles to support product development, manufacturing, and continuous process improvement.

· Develop training and documentation materials, including work instructions, to support production and knowledge transfer.

· Assign support tasks and provide direction to technicians conducting validation and testing activities.

· Train technicians, provide feedback, and coordinate technician activities as required.

· Ensure adherence to applicable quality systems, company procedures, regulatory requirements, and safety standards.

Knowledge & Skills:

· Strong documentation, communication, and interpersonal relationship skills.

· Strong understanding of statistical techniques and their application in quality engineering.

· Working knowledge of IQ/OQ/PQ and equipment/process validation principles.

· Experience working with laboratory and industrial equipment.

· Substantial understanding of engineering principles, theories, and concepts.

· Strong problem-solving, organizational, analytical, and critical thinking skills.

· Thorough understanding of manufacturing processes and equipment.

· Knowledge of and adherence to quality systems and regulatory requirements.

· Strong attention to detail and accuracy.

· Ability to interact professionally with all organizational levels.

· Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

· Ability to work effectively in cross-functional and inter-departmental teams.

· Strong leadership skills and ability to influence change.

· Ability to build and maintain productive internal and external working relationships.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and other computer applications used in engineering and quality functions.

· Familiarity with Six Sigma, Lean, TOPP, and continuous improvement methodologies.

We are seeking an experienced Business Data Analyst to support the planning, execution, reporting and analysis of electric utility inspection programs.

This position supports multiple Distribution and Transmission programs, including detailed asset inspections, annual grid patrols, streetlight patrol surveys, infrared scanning and intrusive pole evaluations.

The Business Data Analyst will work across program management, inspection planning, data analysis and exception processing, partnering with contractors and internal stakeholders to ensure inspection scopes are accurately planned, tracked and completed.

Key Responsibilities

  • Support planning and scheduling for internal and external inspection teams across multiple electric utility programs.

  • Manage schedules covering data collection, processing, contractor deliverables, quality assurance, risk assessment and delivery of inspection results.

  • Develop, maintain and distribute progress and performance reports.

  • Lead and participate in meetings throughout the inspection lifecycle, from initial data collection through risk review and final distribution.

  • Produce regular daily and weekly performance reports, dashboards and ad hoc analyses.

  • Monitor inspection performance and completion against established scopes and deadlines.

  • Analyze financial and cost data and investigate discrepancies identified internally or by contractors.

  • Research data discrepancies across SAP, inspection applications and reporting platforms.

  • Identify synchronization and data-quality issues and coordinate resolution with business and IT teams.

  • Analyze trends in inspection and survey results.

  • Validate that inspection data is accurately populating reporting dashboards.

  • Develop and improve data-management tools that provide timely and accurate status reporting.

  • Use mapping and spatial data to identify potential access constraints and support inspection planning.

  • Create and analyze KMZ files and spatial joins for locations including government lands and other constrained areas.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Accounting, Statistics or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

  • Approximately 5-7 years of analytical experience.

  • Demonstrated ability to perform moderately complex quantitative and data analysis.

  • Experience gathering, documenting and analyzing information and translating findings into actionable conclusions.

  • Strong data-management skills, including data querying, reporting and data controls.

  • Experience developing dashboards and data visualizations.

  • Strong project and issue-tracking capabilities, from identification and root-cause analysis through resolution.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to work across multiple teams, subject matter experts, contractors and stakeholders.

Technical Skills

Experience with several of the following is preferred:

  • SAP

  • Power BI

  • SQL

  • SAS / SAS Visual Analytics

  • Microsoft Excel and MS Office

  • Python

  • Snowflake

  • ArcGIS

  • Data visualization and dashboard development

Experience navigating SAP work orders, maintenance plans, measurement documents, functional locations (FLOCs) and equipment data is particularly relevant.

ArcGIS experience involving the joining and analysis of mapping layers such as districts, functional locations, circuits and constrained areas is also highly desirable.

Work Environment

This is a hybrid position based in Pomona, California, with onsite attendance required Monday and Tuesday. Candidates should be comfortable working across technical, operational and business teams in a data-intensive utility environment.

Location: Draper, UT

Contract Duration: 12 Months

Pay Rate: $52-57/hr



Position Overview

The Senior Manufacturing Engineer will apply advanced engineering knowledge, technical leadership, and manufacturing expertise to improve and sustain manufacturing processes within a highly regulated medical device environment.

This role serves as a technical leader supporting critical implantable component manufacturing operations, with responsibility for driving:

  • Yield improvement
  • Capacity expansion
  • Process robustness
  • Cost reduction
  • Risk mitigation
  • Regulatory and compliance excellence

The successful candidate will use structured problem solving, statistical analysis, Lean Manufacturing, and cross-functional collaboration to resolve complex manufacturing challenges and deliver measurable improvements.

The Senior Manufacturing Engineer will support existing commercial product lines while also contributing to the integration of next-generation products, equipment, and manufacturing technologies.

This position supports 2nd-shift manufacturing operations and requires a high degree of independence, technical ownership, and sound engineering judgment due to limited on-shift engineering support.

Key Responsibilities

1. Manufacturing Performance & Process Improvement

  • Lead complex manufacturing improvement initiatives focused on:
    • Yield stabilization
    • Process capability improvement
    • Capacity expansion
    • Cost reduction
    • Operational risk mitigation
  • Identify, prioritize, and implement process optimization opportunities using:
    • Structured problem-solving methodologies
    • Statistical analysis
    • Lean Manufacturing
    • Continuous improvement principles
  • Serve as a technical leader and subject matter expert for manufacturing processes, equipment, and associated technologies.
  • Partner with Operations, Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and other cross-functional teams to improve manufacturing performance and achieve business objectives.

2. Technical Problem Solving & Compliance

  • Lead investigations and resolution of complex manufacturing, quality, and compliance issues, including:
    • CAPAs
    • Nonconformances
    • Audit observations
    • Process deviations
    • Customer-impacting events
  • Apply data-driven decision-making and statistical techniques to:
    • Evaluate process performance
    • Identify root causes
    • Develop corrective and preventive actions
    • Verify effectiveness of solutions
  • Support regulatory inspections, internal audits, and compliance initiatives as a manufacturing technical expert.

3. Validation, Equipment & Technology Implementation

  • Design and execute:
    • Engineering studies
    • Experiments
    • Process validations
    • Equipment qualifications
  • Develop and execute protocols, analyze results, prepare technical reports, and recommend implementation strategies based on data and risk assessment.
  • Support the introduction and integration of:
    • New products
    • Manufacturing equipment
    • Manufacturing technologies
    • Process improvements
  • Ensure new and existing processes are compliant, manufacturable, and operationally ready.
  • Ensure manufacturing equipment, tooling, fixtures, and processes meet safety, quality, performance, and regulatory requirements.

4. Technical Leadership & Project Execution

  • Lead cross-functional projects from concept through implementation using:
    • Project management tools
    • Risk assessments
    • Structured execution plans
  • Influence engineers, technicians, operations personnel, and business partners without direct authority.
  • Mentor engineers and technicians in:
    • Engineering best practices
    • Manufacturing process control
    • Data analysis
    • Structured problem solving
  • Provide technical direction and training to technicians supporting manufacturing operations and engineering studies.
  • Develop and maintain:
    • Manufacturing documentation
    • Work instructions
    • Procedures
    • Training materials
    • Engineering records
  • Support operational excellence and effective knowledge transfer across the organization.

5. Other Duties

  • Perform other incidental duties as assigned by leadership.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's Degree:

Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a Scientific field with 4+ years of industry or industry/education experience.

Master's Degree:

Master's degree or equivalent in Engineering or a Scientific field with 3+ years of industry or industry/education experience.

Ph.D.:

Ph.D. or equivalent in Engineering or a Scientific field with relevant industry or industry/education experience.

Required Qualifications

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.
  • Proven ability to work independently and exercise sound engineering judgment.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including:
    • Excel
    • PowerPoint
    • Project
  • Knowledge of applicable FDA regulations and quality system requirements.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in an FDA-regulated manufacturing environment, preferably medical device manufacturing.
  • Experience with:
    • CAPA systems
    • Nonconformance investigations
    • Audit support
    • Change control
    • Risk management
  • Experience applying statistical and analytical methodologies, including:
    • Design of Experiments (DOE)
    • Statistical Process Control (SPC)
    • Process capability analysis
    • Hypothesis testing
  • Experience supporting:
    • Process validation
    • Equipment qualification
  • Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional manufacturing improvement projects with measurable business impact.
  • Experience supporting:
    • New product transfers

    • Manufacturing technology integration
  • Experience working with complex manufacturing equipment and automated production systems.

We are seeking an experienced Learning & Development Analyst – Training Evaluation to support the evaluation and measurement of enterprise-wide learning and training programs within the utilities industry.

In this role, you will partner with organizational leaders, subject matter experts, Human Resources, and program stakeholders to develop measurement strategies, assess training effectiveness, and demonstrate the impact of learning programs against business objectives. You will analyze quantitative and qualitative data from multiple sources and translate complex findings into clear, actionable recommendations for stakeholders and senior leadership.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead measurement strategies designed to demonstrate learning program effectiveness and alignment with business objectives.

  • Partner with leaders, program owners, subject matter experts, HR, and other stakeholders to establish training evaluation strategies and success measures.

  • Define performance objectives, metrics, evaluation methodologies, and reporting requirements.

  • Conduct job, task, stakeholder, and learning needs analyses to identify performance gaps and business requirements.

job.title: Senior Mechanical Project Engineer
job.description:
Job Type: Full-Time
Industry: Power Generation / Energy

We are seeking a Senior Owner’s Engineer to provide technical leadership for gas turbine power generation projects from early-stage development through EPC execution, commissioning, and long-term asset optimization.

This is a highly technical, owner-side role for an experienced power-generation engineer with strong knowledge of open-cycle/simple-cycle gas turbines, balance-of-plant systems, equipment integration, EPC execution, and OEM management.

Key Responsibilities

Owner’s Engineering & Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the technical lead and subject matter expert for gas turbine generation projects.
  • Provide owner-side oversight of gas turbines and major auxiliary systems, including fuel gas, lubrication, hydraulics, inlet air, exhaust, cooling, emissions controls, fire protection, and black-start systems.
  • Ensure equipment and plant designs support long-term reliability, availability, maintainability, and operating economics.
  • Manage technical interfaces between the owner, EPC contractor, OEMs, equipment suppliers, and other project stakeholders.

Engineering & Project Development

  • Establish technical requirements, equipment specifications, performance requirements, and project boundary conditions.
  • Lead conceptual design, feasibility studies, technology evaluations, and project development activities.
  • Review and validate engineering deliverables including PFDs, P&IDs, equipment datasheets, specifications, heat and mass balances, and performance calculations.
  • Support selection and evaluation of simple-cycle, combined-cycle, CHP, and emerging power-generation configurations.

Technology & Efficiency

  • Evaluate technologies that improve plant efficiency, flexibility, output, and emissions performance.
  • Support assessments involving inlet air chilling, turbine power augmentation, thermal storage, intercooling, ORC, and other advanced technologies.
  • Lead technical evaluations of emissions-control technologies including SCR and CO/oxidation catalysts.
  • Support decarbonization initiatives, including carbon capture readiness and hydrogen blending.
  • Provide technical input into CAPEX, OPEX, lifecycle economics, and business-case development.

OEM, Procurement & EPC Management

  • Develop technical specifications, RFQs, bid requirements, and performance guarantees for major equipment and EPC contracts.
  • Lead technical evaluations of OEM and EPC proposals.
  • Manage technical deviations, change orders, warranties, and long-term service agreement interfaces.
  • Provide owner-side oversight throughout engineering, procurement, construction, installation, and commissioning.

Risk, Compliance & Permitting

  • Participate in HAZOP, HAZID, and other formal project risk reviews.
  • Identify and mitigate technical, operational, safety, and reliability risks.
  • Support air permitting, emissions modeling, and environmental compliance activities.
  • Ensure projects meet applicable EPA, state/local, environmental, safety, and industry requirements.

Commissioning & Operations

  • Participate in FATs, SATs, startup, commissioning, and performance testing.
  • Lead resolution of technical issues involving OEMs, EPC contractors, and equipment suppliers.
  • Provide ongoing engineering support to operating assets, including troubleshooting, outage planning, performance optimization, upgrades, and reliability improvements.
  • Evaluate retrofit and modernization opportunities to improve efficiency, emissions performance, and long-term asset value.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related engineering discipline.
  • 10+ years of experience in gas turbine power generation, power project development, EPC execution, OEM engineering, or owner/operator environments.
  • Strong technical knowledge of open-cycle/simple-cycle gas turbines and balance-of-plant systems.
  • Experience with gas turbine auxiliaries, equipment integration, and mechanical/piping systems.
  • Experience reviewing PFDs, P&IDs, equipment specifications, datasheets, and thermal/performance documentation.
  • Experience with OEM and EPC contractor management.
  • Knowledge of emissions-control systems and air permitting requirements.
  • Experience supporting project development, procurement, commissioning, or plant operations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working for an IPP, power developer, utility, or owner/operator organization.

job.description:
About the Role



We are looking for a capable and hands-on Financial Accountant to join our team in a role that combines traditional finance responsibilities with ERP implementation and business systems support.

This is an exciting opportunity for someone who enjoys more than just the numbers. Alongside supporting core accounting and finance functions, you will play an important role in the implementation and optimisation of our ERP environment, including Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations (D365 F&O) or a similar ERP platform.

You will work closely with Finance, Operations, IT and external implementation partners to help ensure that our new systems, processes and reporting are fit for purpose.

The ideal candidate will be a strong accountant who is also systems-minded, analytical, organised and comfortable working through problems and testing new processes.

Key Responsibilities



Finance & Accounting

  • Support day-to-day financial accounting and finance operations.
  • Assist with month-end and year-end close processes.
  • Prepare and review account reconciliations and financial reports.
  • Assist with general ledger, journals, accruals, prepayments and other accounting activities.
  • Support accounts payable and accounts receivable processes as required.
  • Assist with budgeting, forecasting and management reporting.
  • Identify opportunities to improve financial processes, controls and reporting.
  • Maintain accurate financial records and ensure compliance with relevant accounting standards and internal policies.



ERP Implementation & Systems

  • Support the implementation, configuration and optimisation of Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations or a similar ERP system.
  • Work with Finance and business stakeholders to understand current processes and future requirements.
  • Assist in translating finance requirements into practical system and process solutions.
  • Participate in User Acceptance Testing (UAT), including preparing test scenarios, executing test scripts and documenting results.
  • Identify, investigate and help resolve system issues, data issues and process gaps.
  • Validate financial transactions, workflows, reporting and integrations within the ERP.
  • Assist with data migration activities, including data validation and reconciliation.
  • Review and document business processes and system procedures.
  • Work with implementation partners, consultants and internal stakeholders to track issues through to resolution.
  • Support system cutover, go-live and post-implementation activities.
  • Help develop user guides, process documentation and training materials.
  • Act as a key link between the Finance team and ERP/IT stakeholders.



About You

We are looking for someone who combines strong accounting fundamentals with an interest in technology and business systems.

You will ideally have:

  • Relevant accounting qualifications or significant accounting experience.
  • Experience working in a Financial Accountant or similar finance role.
  • Strong understanding of general ledger, month-end close, reconciliations and financial reporting.
  • Experience with an ERP system such as Microsoft Dynamics 365, Dynamics AX, SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Pronto, TechnologyOne or a similar platform.
  • An understanding of ERP implementation, system upgrades or process improvement would be highly desirable.
  • Experience with UAT, system testing, requirements gathering or data validation would be advantageous.
  • Strong Excel skills and confidence working with financial data.
  • Excellent attention to detail and a methodical approach to problem solving.
  • The ability to understand both finance processes and how those processes translate into an ERP system.
  • Strong communication skills and the confidence to work with Finance, IT, Operations and external consultants.
  • A proactive attitude and willingness to get involved and solve problems rather than simply identify them.



What We Offer

  • A broad and varied role across Finance and business systems.
  • The opportunity to play a key role in an ERP transformation.
  • Exposure to Microsoft Dynamics 365 and modern finance technology.
  • The opportunity to work closely with senior Finance, Operations and IT stakeholders.
  • A role with genuine scope to improve processes and ways of working.
  • Support and development as you build your ERP and systems expertise.

Position Overview

The Manufacturing Engineer applies engineering theory and principles to solve problems related to industrial layout, manufacturing processes, production, and operational efficiency.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience with manufacturing processes, engineering drawings, blueprints, production standards, quality assurance, and process improvement. The role requires the ability to analyze production data, evaluate workflows, and collaborate with management and engineering teams to improve efficiency, quality, and reliability.

  • Collaborate with management and engineering personnel to establish and maintain quality and reliability standards.

    • Workflow and routing
    • Manufacturing floor layouts
    • Material handling processes

  • Observe employees operating manufacturing equipment to verify that equipment is being operated and maintained in accordance with quality and safety standards.
  • Conduct time and motion observations using appropriate timing devices to determine task completion times and evaluate fatigue factors.
  • Analyze production and operational data to identify trends, inefficiencies, and deviations from established standards.
  • Prepare technical reports and documentation to validate existing standards or identify areas requiring improvement.

Required Skills & Qualifications

  • Strong creativity, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a team.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Ability to perform common engineering calculations and computations.
  • Ability to create sketches and engineering drawings.
  • Proficiency in reading and interpreting:
    • Blueprints
    • Technical drawings
    • Schematics
    • Computer-generated reports

Education & Experience

  • 5–7 years of relevant manufacturing engineering experience required.

job.title: Principal Engineer
job.description:
Principal Engineer (CAPA)

Location: Draper, UT

Schedule: Standard

Contract Duration: 12 Months

Max Pay Rate: $58-63/hour



Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Quality Engineer / CAPA professional to take ownership of complex, high-visibility Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA) activities while helping improve and accelerate the overall CAPA process across the site.

This role will provide technical guidance to CAPA personnel, including contract Senior Quality Engineers, while ensuring investigations, corrective action plans, documentation, and effectiveness checks meet quality system requirements.

The successful candidate will have strong knowledge of CAPA processes, Quality Management Systems (QMS), regulatory requirements, risk management, and audit readiness within a regulated environment.



Key Responsibilities

CAPA Management & Leadership

  • Take ownership of designated high-complexity and high-visibility CAPAs from investigation through closure.
  • Drive improvements and acceleration of the overall CAPA process across the site portfolio.
  • Provide guidance, coaching, and day-to-day technical direction to CAPA personnel, including contract Senior Quality Engineers.
  • Balance workload across CAPA resources and review:
    • Investigations
    • Corrective action plans
    • Preventive actions
    • Effectiveness checks
  • Review CAPA records for completeness and quality before routing for approval.

CAPA Review Board Support

  • Support the CAPA Chair in preparing materials for CAPA Review Board meetings.
  • Pre-screen CAPA records to ensure they are ready for board review.
  • Present CAPA portfolio status, aging, and key issues to stakeholders.
  • Track and follow up on CAPA Review Board decisions, action items, and commitments through completion.

Quality System & Compliance

  • Support updates and modifications to the site's Quality Management System (QMS).
  • Lead or approve revisions to:
    • CAPA procedures
    • Templates
    • Work instructions
    • Training materials
  • Perform gap assessments against applicable quality and regulatory requirements, including:
    • ISO 13485
    • 21 CFR 820 / QMSR
    • MDSAP
  • Ensure CAPA processes remain aligned with regulatory and quality system expectations.

Documentation & Audit Readiness

  • Ensure documentation compliance across the CAPA subsystem.
  • Maintain accurate and complete CAPA records with strong:
    • Record integrity
    • Traceability
    • Documentation practices
  • Ensure both closed and active CAPA records remain audit-ready.
  • Identify documentation gaps and drive appropriate corrective actions.

Risk Management & Systemic Issue Assessment

  • Apply risk-based decision-making when evaluating systemic nonconformities.
  • Assess potential impacts to:
    • Quality Management System
    • Products
    • Processes
    • Regulatory compliance
  • Determine the appropriate scope and depth of corrective actions based on risk and potential impact.
  • Ensure CAPA activities address systemic issues rather than only individual occurrences.

Quality System Integration

  • Connect CAPA outcomes with other quality system processes, including:
    • Customer complaints
    • Nonconformances (NCs)
    • Internal and external audit findings
    • Risk management
    • Management Review
  • Identify relationships between quality events and systemic issues.
  • Drive appropriate actions to close identified quality system gaps.

Audit & Inspection Support – Preferred

  • Serve as a CAPA Subject Matter Expert (SME) during:
    • FDA inspections
    • Notified Body audits
    • Customer audits
  • Defend CAPA records and explain investigation and corrective action decisions.
  • Support the preparation and negotiation of audit responses.
  • Manage audit-related CAPA commitments and follow-up activities through closure.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering is required.
  • 8–10 years of relevant professional experience required.
  • Strong experience managing complex CAPA investigations and corrective action activities.
  • Experience working within a regulated Quality Management System.
  • Strong understanding of risk-based quality decision-making.
  • Experience with quality system documentation, compliance, and audit readiness.
  • Strong communication, leadership, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to provide technical direction and guidance to other quality professionals.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience supporting FDA inspections and regulatory audits.
  • Experience with ISO 13485, 21 CFR 820/QMSR, and MDSAP.

job.title: GSE Build Technician II
job.description:
GSE Build Technician II

Hydrogen Group is hiring on behalf of a confidential client, a leading aerospace and advanced manufacturing organization supporting complex vehicle production, testing, and launch operations.

Position Overview

We are seeking a GSE Build Technician II to support the fabrication, installation, maintenance, testing, and troubleshooting of ground support equipment (GSE) used across rocket production, test, and launch environments.

This is a hands-on Level II technician position requiring the ability to independently execute assigned work with limited supervision. The role will work closely with Engineering, Test Operations, Launch Operations, Quality, EH&S, and other technical teams to construct and maintain mechanical systems, fluid systems, test infrastructure, launch equipment, and related facility systems.

The work may involve stainless-steel tubing and piping, valves, regulators, instrumentation, manifolds, structural components, hydraulic and pneumatic equipment, high-pressure gas and cryogenic systems, pumps, and other mechanical GSE.

Technicians at this level are expected to take ownership of assigned scopes—from reviewing technical documentation and gathering the appropriate tools and materials through fabrication, installation, troubleshooting, testing, and final documentation. The ability to identify and address routine issues independently, while knowing when to involve Engineering, Quality, EH&S, or leadership, is essential.

This position is based at a rocket production facility in Briggs, Texas, north of Cedar Park.

Key Responsibilities

  • Independently execute GSE fabrication, installation, maintenance, repair, troubleshooting, modification, and upgrade activities across production, test, launch, and facility environments.
  • Build mechanical and fluid assemblies using released engineering drawings and technical documentation, including tubing, piping, valves, regulators, gauges, instrumentation, manifolds, panels, structural supports, and related components.
  • Prepare, measure, bend, route, fit, and install stainless-steel tubing and piping using approved fabrication practices.
  • Assemble and install a variety of mechanical and fluid-system interfaces, including compression fittings, NPT, AN/MS-style connections, flanges, and other approved connection types.
  • Select and install appropriate fittings, seals, fasteners, and related hardware based on system requirements.
  • Perform torque and controlled-fastener installation using calibrated equipment while maintaining proper component orientation, accessibility, cleanliness, support, and overall workmanship.
  • Interpret mechanical drawings, fabrication and assembly documentation, schematics, P&IDs, work instructions, and other technical information to execute assigned work and verify installed configurations.
  • Identify discrepancies between field conditions and engineering requirements and communicate issues through the appropriate channels.
  • Prepare for upcoming work by determining required tooling, materials, hardware, consumables, access equipment, and other resources.
  • Coordinate concurrent activities and plan work efficiently to reduce equipment or operational downtime.
  • Conduct visual and dimensional inspections, troubleshooting, leak checks, flushing, cleaning, commissioning, system verification, and other qualified testing activities.
  • Assist with high-pressure gas, cryogenic, hydraulic, pneumatic, pump, valve, and other stored-energy systems, including hydrostatic and pneumatic testing when properly trained and authorized.
  • Adhere to established requirements for pressure systems, exclusion zones, barricades, stored energy, lockout/tagout (LOTO), FOD, ESD, PPE, contamination control, cleanliness, and other applicable safety and quality procedures.
  • Escalate technical, safety, quality, or operational concerns to Engineering, Quality, EH&S, or leadership when appropriate.
  • Provide field feedback regarding constructability, maintainability, accessibility, and system operability.
  • Support construction, modification, commissioning, verification, maintenance, and upgrade work at test stands and launch facilities.
  • Participate in rigging, crane, forklift, aerial-lift, and other material-handling activities when appropriately trained and qualified.
  • Maintain clean, organized, test-ready workspaces and complete required inspections of equipment and work areas.
  • Record completed work, installation details, photographs, discrepancies, constraints, and open actions within JIRA or other designated electronic work-management platforms.
  • Work collaboratively with other technicians and functional groups and provide hands-on guidance and informal mentorship to Level I technicians.
  • Contribute ideas and participate in continuous improvement efforts related to tooling, fabrication techniques, work sequencing, organization, and execution processes.
  • Provide hands-on support for Test and Launch activities as directed by the applicable operations or engineering teams.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent.
  • At least 3 years of professional hands-on experience in mechanical fabrication, maintenance, aerospace, aviation, military, industrial construction, process piping, or a related technical discipline.
  • Proven ability to independently perform mechanical fabrication, assembly, installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting work.
  • Proficiency with hand tools, power tools, calibrated/torque tools, and basic precision measurement equipment.
  • Ability to interpret and work from mechanical drawings, fabrication or assembly drawings, schematics, P&IDs, work instructions, and similar technical documentation.
  • Practical experience with tubing, piping, valves, fittings, hydraulic or pneumatic equipment, process equipment, or comparable mechanical fluid systems.
  • Understanding of workmanship standards, configuration control, cleanliness, safety practices, and technical documentation requirements.
  • Ability to organize and execute routine assignments without constant oversight, recognize areas of technical uncertainty, and obtain clarification rather than making unapproved changes.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across multiple technical and operational teams.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities while maintaining a strong focus on safety and quality.
  • Ability to safely lift a minimum of 30 pounds, remain standing for extended periods, and work in industrial, production, test-stand, launch-site, and outdoor environments.
  • Ability and willingness to travel to project locations as needed.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Associate degree in engineering technology, mechanical technology, aviation maintenance, welding, industrial technology, or a related technical field.
  • A&P license, relevant trade certification, or advanced military technical training.
  • Previous experience in aerospace GSE, launch operations, rocket testing, aviation maintenance, military maintenance, oil and gas, semiconductor/high-purity environments, chemical or process facilities, power generation, shipyards, or industrial mechanical construction.
  • Hands-on experience fabricating stainless-steel tubing, including manual tube bending and tube preparation.
  • Experience working with Swagelok or comparable compression-fitting systems.
  • Familiarity with NPT, AN, MS, flange, Grayloc, or similar fluid-system connections and welded tubing/piping assemblies.
  • Experience working with high-pressure gas, cryogenic, hydraulic, pneumatic, oxygen-clean/high-purity systems, pressure testing, hydrostatic proof testing, pneumatic leak testing, or system commissioning.
  • Exposure to orbital tube welding processes or associated preparation requirements.
  • Experience operating or working around cranes, rigging equipment, forklifts, telehandlers, boom lifts, or similar material-handling equipment.
  • Experience managing controlled hazardous energy, LOTO, pressurized systems, and other stored-energy hazards.
  • Familiarity with ASME B31.3 or comparable industrial piping standards.
  • Experience using JIRA, electronic work-order platforms, MES, SAP, Maximo, Confluence, Microsoft Office, or similar systems.
  • Experience creating photographic installation records or other documentation used for configuration control.

  • Use AutoCAD, Revit, and Navisworks to develop coordinated, construction-ready drawings and models. Lead BIM coordination efforts with other trades and identify potential clashes before they impact field installation.
  • Conduct constructability reviews and identify potential installation challenges, access limitations, sequencing issues, and productivity concerns during the design phase.
  • Work with field operations and prefabrication teams to incorporate modularization, fabrication, and labor-efficiency considerations into design and modeling processes.
  • Assist with value engineering efforts by identifying practical, cost-conscious design alternatives while maintaining project performance, safety, and quality requirements.
  • Coordinate with Project Managers, Estimating, Operations, and other stakeholders to ensure engineering and BIM deliverables support project schedules, budgets, procurement activities, and construction sequencing.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop BIM Engineers, Designers, and VDC personnel, including workload allocation, technical development, and performance support.
  • Establish and maintain consistent modeling standards, coordination procedures, and quality-control practices across projects.
  • Participate in design reviews, coordination sessions, and client meetings, providing technical guidance throughout both preconstruction and project execution.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s or Associate’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Construction Technology, or a related field, or equivalent hands-on experience in electrical construction.
  • 5+ years of experience supporting electrical construction projects within BIM, VDC, engineering, or design-build environments.

  • Strong understanding of high-voltage substation design practices and engineering documentation.
  • Experience coordinating external engineering consultants and/or Engineers of Record.
  • Knowledge of relevant industry codes and standards, including IEEE and NESC.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to coordinate across engineering, project management, construction and external stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in Engineering or an MBA.

Contract Details

Location: Remote, with bimonthly reporting to Juno Beach, FL
Duration: 12-month contract
Pay Rate: Up to $67.94/hour
Travel: Travel within North America required

job.title: Robotics Engineer
job.description:
Robotics Engineer – NACHI / FANUC




LOCATION: Toledo, OH → Normal, IL - both onsite

SCHEDULE: 60 hours/week, 12-hour shifts; rotating AM/PM

DURATION: 3-month initial contract

PAY: 51-56 USD per hour

IMPORTANT: Candidates will spend approximately 2–3 months in Toledo, OH before transitioning to Normal, IL. This is an onsite position at both locations.



Job Responsibilities:

In this role, you will be responsible for the programming, integration, commissioning, and optimization of robotic arc welding systems within an automotive Bodyshop environment. You will work primarily with FANUC and NACHI robotic platforms to support MIG welding applications and ensure production-ready, repeatable processes.

Key responsibilities include:

· Programming and integrating NACHI and FANUC robots for automotive body-in-white (BIW) applications.

· Developing and optimizing complex MIG welding paths and robotic trajectories.

· Configuring and fine-tuning welding parameters to achieve consistent weld quality and minimize defects.

· Supporting robotic system integration from initial programming and commissioning through production startup.

· Optimizing robotic welding processes to reduce spatter, thermal distortion, and cycle times.

· Establishing and following robotic programming standards based on process requirements and application types.

· Supporting the structural and geometric integrity of BIW sub-assemblies through accurate and repeatable robotic welding processes.

· Troubleshooting robot, welding, hardware, software, and process-related issues in a high-volume automotive production environment.

Essential Duties and Job Functions:

· Program and refine complex MIG welding trajectories on NACHI robots.

· Optimize torch positioning, including work and travel angles and electrode stick-out.

· Configure welding parameter schedules directly on robotic controllers.

· Troubleshoot and eliminate welding defects including porosity, lack of fusion, undercut, and excessive burn-through.

· Develop and maintain automatic Tool Center Point (TCP) check routines.

· Perform TCP maintenance and calibration following consumable changes, including contact tips, nozzles, and goosenecks.

· Maintain accurate and documented backup and version-control procedures for robot controllers.

· Create and maintain periodic image backups of robotic controller systems.

· Program and configure FANUC robots using ArcTool, including weld schedules, torch control, and tool coordinate systems.

· Program and configure NACHI FD/AX series controllers for MIG/arc welding applications.

· Configure power-source interfaces and synchronize robot travel speed with wire feed rates.

· Integrate and maintain welding peripherals, including torch cleaning stations, reamers, wire cutters, neck aligners, and automated TCP calibration equipment.

· Configure communication interfaces including Digital/Analog, DeviceNet, and EtherNet/IP.

· Integrate robotic systems with welding power sources including Fronius TPS/i, Lincoln Electric, and Miller equipment.

· Implement and maintain robot safety systems, including FANUC Dual Check Safety (DCS) and NACHI RMU (Robot Monitoring Unit).

· Support robotic commissioning, startup, and production readiness activities.

· Perform rapid root-cause analysis and troubleshooting during high-volume automotive production.

· Collaborate with PLC programmers, mechanical designers, weld quality inspectors, maintenance technicians, and other engineering teams.

Knowledge & Skills:

· Advanced knowledge of FANUC robot programming and ArcTool.

· Strong hands-on experience programming and integrating NACHI robots.

· Strong understanding of NACHI FD/AX series controllers and arc applications.

· Deep knowledge of MIG/MAG welding processes and robotic welding applications.

· Strong understanding of welding parameters, including voltage, amperage, wire feed speed, and shielding gas flow.

· Knowledge of welding transfer modes, including short-circuit, globular, spray, and pulsed arc.

· Experience integrating robotic welding systems with industrial power sources.

· Knowledge of Fronius, Lincoln Electric, and/or Miller welding systems.

· Experience with Digital/Analog, DeviceNet, and EtherNet/IP communication interfaces.

· Experience integrating welding peripherals and automated TCP calibration systems.

· Knowledge of FANUC DCS and NACHI RMU safety systems.

· Strong troubleshooting and root-cause analysis skills.

· Ability to work effectively in a high-pressure, high-volume automotive production environment.

· Strong cross-functional collaboration and communication skills.

· Ability to work with PLC programmers, mechanical engineers/designers, weld quality teams, and maintenance personnel.

· Professional working proficiency in English.

· Ability to work extended hours and rotating 12-hour shifts as required.

Education & Experience:

· Bachelor's degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Automation, Welding, Electromechanical Engineering, or a related field.

· Minimum of 5 years of hands-on experience programming and integrating FANUC and NACHI robots.

· Minimum of 2 years of experience with MIG welding applications.

· Experience working with robotic welding systems in an automotive BIW/Bodyshop environment.

· Demonstrated experience integrating robotic systems from initial programming through commissioning and production startup.

· Experience with FANUC ArcTool programming is required.

· Experience with NACHI robotic programming and integration is required.

· Experience with welding power-source integration and robotic peripherals is highly desirable.

· Experience with robot safety systems, including FANUC DCS and NACHI RMU, is preferred.

· Experience troubleshooting robotic welding systems in a high-volume manufacturing environment is highly desirable.

The Prototype Trim Technician - Seat Laboratory is responsible for accurately cutting, sewing, and assembling seat trim covers, and for participating in the complete seat build process.

  • Verify fit, finish, and functional operation (adjusters, recliners, headrests, etc.) of completed seats.

  • Follow standard operating procedures, quality standards, and inspection criteria for trim covers and seat assemblies.
  • Document production results, defects, and rework in the appropriate systems or forms.
  • Escalate quality issues, equipment concerns, and process deviations promptly.

  • Provide feedback on patterns, methods, and tooling to improve build quality and efficiency.
  • Support trials, prototypes, and engineering changes for new seat designs and materials.
  • Collaborate with engineering, quality, and production teams to resolve build issues and implement best practices.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience in seat trim sewing, upholstery, automotive interiors, furniture upholstery, or closely related manufacturing/production work.

  • Experience assembling complete seats or similar upholstered assemblies from component level to finished product.

Skills & Competencies

Technical Skills

  • Proficiency operating industrial sewing machines and related equipment (cutters, skivers, binders, sergers, etc.).
  • Ability to read and interpret patterns, drawings, work instructions, and digital layouts.
  • Comfortable using basic manufacturing software and equipment interfaces, such as:
    • Pattern or nesting software for cut planning (Optitex or equivalent).
    • HMI screens or terminals to retrieve work orders and record production data.
    • Basic office or manufacturing systems for training, quality, and reporting.

Quality & Craftsmanship

  • Strong attention to detail in stitch quality, seam alignment, and appearance.
  • Ability to perform self-inspection and correct defects at the source.

Problem Solving & Collaboration

  • Ability to identify fit, finish, and functional build issues and work with cross-functional teams (engineering, quality, production) to resolve them quickly.

job.description:
Senior BESS Engineer – Sizing & Battery Technology

Location: Juno Beach, FL – Hybrid
Contract: 12 Months
Pay Rate: Up to $52.96 per hour

We are seeking an experienced Senior BESS Engineer to support a Utility Scale Energy Storage team, providing technical expertise across battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing, optimization, battery technology and power conversion systems (PCS).

This position will serve as a technical Subject Matter Expert supporting utility-scale energy storage projects and the evaluation of existing and emerging storage technologies.

The successful candidate will combine strong engineering fundamentals with hands-on BESS sizing experience and an innovative approach to engineering tools, automation, data analytics and emerging technologies.

BESS Sizing & Optimization

  • Provide technical leadership for utility-scale BESS sizing methodologies, assumptions, optimization and project-specific sizing decisions.

  • Develop and optimize end-to-end BESS sizing from the point of interconnection through GSU/substation, PCS/inverters, DC systems and battery equipment.

  • Account for system losses, battery degradation, augmentation and overbuild strategies, temperature effects, operating constraints and contractual requirements.

  • Ensure sizing solutions align with power purchase agreements and project-specific technical requirements.

  • Develop, maintain and continuously improve BESS sizing methodologies, calculators, assumptions and technical guidance.

  • Maintain accurate records of sizing inputs, assumptions, technical decisions and results throughout project development and execution.

  • Review project-specific sizing results and identify optimization opportunities, risks and potential improvements.

  • Provide sizing recommendations to Engineering, Development, Supply Chain and project teams.

  • Maintain sizing tools and equipment databases to incorporate current BESS and PCS ratings and technical characteristics.

Battery & Energy Storage Technology Evaluation

  • Evaluate existing and emerging battery technologies for utility-scale applications.

  • Perform technical assessments covering degradation, efficiency, available energy, reliability, state of charge (SOC) and state of health (SOH).

  • Evaluate battery performance from cell and module level through complete system applications.

  • Assess emerging and alternative energy storage technologies for new use cases and regional market requirements.

  • Evaluate technologies based on technical maturity, performance, safety, scalability, supply chain readiness and commercial viability.

  • Develop preliminary system sizing and CAPEX estimates for alternative energy storage technologies.

  • Support technology selection, business-case development, pilot projects and commercial deployment decisions.

  • Analyze vendor RFP and RFI information to track technology developments, product roadmaps, performance and commercial readiness.

  • Summarize technical findings and provide recommendations to engineering and management teams.

Digital Engineering, Automation & AI

  • Develop and improve engineering tools used for BESS sizing, technical evaluations and battery performance forecasting.

  • Automate repetitive engineering calculations and workflows where appropriate.

  • Apply data analytics and software-based tools to improve engineering productivity, consistency and decision-making.

  • Utilize tools such as Excel/VBA, Python, Power BI, low-code platforms and AI-assisted engineering applications where appropriate.

  • Identify practical applications for emerging technologies and AI within energy storage engineering.

  • Partner with software development and technical teams to translate engineering methodologies into scalable digital tools and automated workflows.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • Demonstrated experience with utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS).

  • Strong expertise in BESS sizing and optimization, including AC/DC sizing, system losses, degradation, augmentation/overbuild strategies, thermal impacts and project-specific operating requirements.

  • Knowledge of battery technologies and utility-scale energy storage system architecture.

  • Experience evaluating battery and/or PCS technologies.

  • Strong analytical and engineering problem-solving skills.

  • Excellent project management, communication and organizational capabilities.

  • Ability to communicate complex technical findings and recommendations across engineering and business teams.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience with emerging or alternative storage technologies such as flow batteries, multi-day energy storage, sodium-ion batteries, fuel-cell-like technologies or supercapacitors.

  • Knowledge of power electronics, including PCS/inverters, IGBT and SiC technologies.

  • Experience working with major or emerging battery and PCS suppliers.

  • Experience applying Python, Excel/VBA, Power BI, automation, AI or advanced data analytics to engineering applications.

  • Experience developing engineering calculation, sizing or performance-prediction tools.

  • Understanding of utility-scale energy storage commercial and project requirements.

  • Strong interest in emerging battery technologies and continuously improving existing engineering processes.

Some travel to battery manufacturing facilities may be required to support technology assessments.
